title: Building multiplication proofs inside Heyting arithmetic

based_on.title: Logic and Proof, §17.4 Defining Arithmetic Operations (HTML version 3.18.4)
based_on.pages: §17.4 multiplication clauses and listed exercises (distributivity, zero/one, associativity/commutativity); §18.3 exercise1

summary: Construct finite HA multiplication proofs by induction and addition rearrangements, then instantiate distributivity, commutativity and associativity at arbitrary terms.
abstract: Expanding a product whose factors contain unknowns should not require calculating those unknowns. The recursion equations for multiplication let us extend a product by one successor, but they do not list the familiar rearrangement laws. Using the proved addition identities, we construct zero and one on the left, commutativity, distributivity and associativity as finite deductions inside Heyting arithmetic. Keeping the other variables fixed in each induction makes those universal proofs apply to arbitrary arithmetic terms and to equations supplied under additional assumptions. A doubling calculation and an equation expansion illustrate these proof operations, while a two-element structure shows why the four recursion clauses alone do not already give left zero.
